articles.text:
Helical Fusion Raises $20.6 Million In Series B Second Close With Fuji Electric And Other Investors
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Helical Fusion Raises $20.6 Million In Series B Second Close With Fuji Electric And Other Investors
Helical Fusion raised JPY 3.23 billion, or approximately $20.6 million, in the second close of its Series B financing as it advances development of its commercial fusion program. Fuji Electric joined the round as both a strategic investor and an Official Partner of Helical Fusion’s Helix Program.
Additional investors included Hazama Ando, Fujikura, Tokyo Gas, KKT, Urata, Kepple Group, and Ecrowd NEXT, along with other corporate and individual investors.
Including grants, loans, and other financing, Helical Fusion’s cumulative funding has reached approximately JPY 13.15 billion, or $83.8 million.
The company plans to use the new capital to accelerate the Helix Program, its roadmap toward commercially viable fusion power.
Helical Fusion is developing Helix HARUKA, an integrated demonstration device, and Helix KANATA, which is intended to become its first fusion power plant capable of net-electricity generation in the 2030s.
Construction of Helix HARUKA is underway at the National Institute for Fusion Science campus in Toki City, Japan.
More than 30 Japanese companies are participating in development and manufacturing for the project.
Fuji Electric and Helical Fusion began working together in 2025 when Fuji Electric agreed to supply power equipment for Helical Fusion’s high-temperature superconducting magnet development.
The expanded relationship will include collaboration on products, services, and technologies required for future fusion power systems.
KEY QUOTES:
“The Helix Program is steadily moving forward. At the Helix HARUKA construction site, our team and industrial partners are working together every day to turn fusion technology into real hardware.”
“Japan has accumulated nearly 70 years of knowledge in Helical Stellarator research and has one of the world’s strongest manufacturing and engineering ecosystems. We intend to bring these strengths together to realize commercial fusion power and create a new global energy industry.”
Takaya Taguchi, Co-Founder and CEO of Helical Fusion

articles.title: Polyphron Raises $20M to Predict Drug Toxicity in Human Tissue Before Clinical Trials
articles.snippet: An MRI in late 2023 found a mass on Matthew Osman's pancreas. It turned out to be benign, but the months of not knowing made him ask why medicine still cannot predict what happens inside the human body. Today, his company Polyphron grows living human heart tissue in an automated foundry and uses it to teach AI what a drug will do next, backed by a fresh $20M. Find out why Osman believes the real bottleneck in AI-driven biology has nothing to do with generating ideas.
